data.revised_prompt: The four-arm X-shaped skeleton with four circular motor mounts in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The centered top-down framing and scale of the airframe plan in <Picture 1> is <Subject 2>. The target image transforms <Subject 1> into a photorealistic 8K industrial design rendering of a quadcopter with a stretched X-shaped layout, streamlined fuselage, and propellers while maintaining <Subject 2>, replacing the flat dark background from <Picture 1> with a studio surface under soft overhead lighting. <Subject 1> is partially preserved; the exact positions, angles, and proportions of its four arms and four circular motor mounts remain, while its flat grey vector shapes change into three-dimensional carbon fiber foldable arms with modular quick-release connectors and reinforced anodized aluminum motor covers. <Subject 2> is fully preserved. The central intersection of <Subject 1> connects to a newly introduced streamlined fuselage featuring a 60-degree edge angle, a cold grey color scheme, an anodized aluminum honeycomb grille, and a discreetly integrated GPS antenna on its top surface. A glowing blue LED light band traces the fuselage contours. Four large ABS propellers with a glossy nano-coating and a 35-degree rotor blade angle are mounted atop the motor housings at the tips of <Subject 1>, spanning a 30-centimeter rotor-to-rotor distance with an 80-centimeter wing curvature radius. Soft 5500K overhead lighting casts crisp, high-contrast shadows beneath the raised arms, fuselage, and spinning propeller blades onto the neutral dark matte studio floor.
